contract.title: Personal API tokens with read and write scopes
contract.objective:
Customers want to sync with their CRM, so let people create personal API tokens. Store them in a new table `api_tokens` through a migration. `POST /api/tokens` with `{ name, scope }` (scope `read` or `write`; 400 `invalid_name` or `invalid_scope`) answers 201 `{ token: { id, name, scope, createdAt, lastUsedAt, revokedAt }, secret }`: the secret is shown only then and never stored, only a hash of it. `GET /api/tokens` lists your own tokens (never a secret or hash) and `DELETE /api/tokens/:id` revokes one of yours (204; 404 for anyone else's). On /api routes, `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` acts as the token's owner, seeing exactly what they see; a `read` token may only make GET requests (403 `insufficient_scope` otherwise, changing nothing); an unknown or revoked token gets 401. A token cannot list, create or revoke tokens (403), and HTML pages ignore tokens. Each use records `lastUsedAt`. Creating and revoking are audited (`token.created`, `token.revoked`) without the secret. Add tests, including the refusals.

Work in this repository as its CLAUDE.md describes, and add tests for every rule you add.
